description: KernelCrew is a builder-driven team focused on turning raw Earth observation data into fast, actionable web tools. Rooted in systems engineering, data analytics (Python, R, SQL), and rapid prototyping, we thrive in high-pace hackathon environments where shipping a working product matters most.
summary: Fire Relay South America turns 26 years of NASA FIRMS active-fire detections into one comparable monthly burning calendar for South America. The FIRMS record is a relay of five instruments (MODIS Terra/Aqua, VIIRS S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21). They have different footprints and overpass times, so simply adding them creates false fire trends at each sensor transition. We processed 85,002,288 raw detections (2000-11 to 2026-11) into 75,556,207 quality-controlled detections. We removed static industrial sources and volcanoes and flagged South Atlantic Magnetic Anomaly artifacts. Then we learned the sensor-to-sensor relationship on a frozen 2012–2020 overlap with leakage-free 200 km spatial validation. Our harmonization model raises R² from 0.35 to 0.82 and cuts the step jumps at sensor transitions by 92.8%. Country, Admin-1 and continental totals match exactly. A bilingual (EN/ES) web app lets users compare any month against a frozen 2001–2020 climatology. It also shows statistically controlled trends and 90-day early-season signals, maps 50 km and 10 km cells, and exports data in one click. This matters because fire managers and scientists need long records where a change in the satellite is not mistaken for a change in fire activity.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Fire Relay South America is an interactive fire seasonality observatory covering 14 South American countries and 243 first-level administrative units, from November 2000 to November 2026.

It helps answer key questions: Is the current month's fire activity unusual compared with the 2001–2020 baseline? Is the fire season starting earlier than expected? Which regions exhibit statistically significant long-term trends? Where is fire activity geographically concentrated?

HOW IT WORKS

1. Data Processing and Quality Control

We processed 85,002,288 NASA FIRMS detections from MODIS C6.1, VIIRS S-NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21. Data cleaning was performed out-of-core using DuckDB and Parquet. The pipeline removes volcanoes, offshore detections, and static sources; masks 358 persistent industrial cells at 10 km resolution; repairs invalid FRP values; flags potential South Atlantic Magnetic Anomaly false alarms; and merges repeated detections from the same satellite overpass. Finally, detections are aggregated into equal-area 10 km and 50 km grids.

2. Cross-Sensor Harmonization

We evaluated four harmonization approaches: M0 (raw observations), M1 (physical bridge), M2 (hurdle Tweedie model with covariate-shift weighting), and M3 (blending, Kalman relay, and non-negative hierarchical reconciliation).

Models were trained exclusively on the 2012–2020 MODIS/VIIRS overlap period and evaluated using frozen 200 km spatial validation blocks to prevent spatial leakage.

Our final model, M3, improves R² from 0.35 to 0.82 and reduces artificial discontinuities across the 2002, 2012, 2018, 2021, and 2023 satellite transitions by 92.8%. It also maintains consistency between administrative, national, and continental totals within a numerical tolerance of 1e-9.

3. Fire Seasonality and Climate Analytics

The observatory combines a frozen 2001–2020 climatological baseline, Theil–Sen trend estimation, the Hamed–Rao autocorrelation-corrected Mann–Kendall test, Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate control, L-moment GEV extreme-value screening, and a trailing 90-day early-onset detection method.

4. Interactive Web Application

An offline-capable, bilingual (English/Spanish) application provides:

  • Month-by-month interactive fire maps with playback controls and fixed or monthly color scales.
  • Annual fire seasonality calendars.
  • Historical time series with 90% uncertainty bands.
  • Early-onset detection curves.
  • An audit table showing data maturity and active satellite regimes.
  • One-click CSV exports.

Every map view explicitly identifies the active sensors, indicates whether observations are partial or near-real-time, and distinguishes harmonized 50 km estimates from raw 10 km detection counts.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Fire Relay South America provides researchers, environmental agencies, and land managers with a consistent long-term record of fire activity across South America. By accounting for changes in satellite instrumentation, it helps prevent sensor transitions from being mistaken for actual changes in fire activity.

Scientific limitations and methodological constraints are openly documented in docs/validation/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md.

The platform is designed for scientific, environmental, and climatological analysis, not tactical firefighting.

TECHNOLOGIES

Python 3.12, DuckDB, Polars, PyArrow, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, LightGBM, statsmodels, GeoPandas, Shapely, PyProj, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Docker, and Google Cloud Run.

The entire development and model-training workflow was executed locally on CPU hardware, without requiring a GPU.

CREATIVITY AND FACTORS CONSIDERED

Rather than treating satellite transitions as a mapping problem, we approached them as a cross-sensor calibration and harmonization challenge.

Particular attention was given to spatial leakage prevention, uncertainty quantification, geographic consistency, sensor-regime transparency, and reproducibility.

The complete pipeline can be rebuilt with a single command, and 50 automated tests cover data processing, model validation, API behavior, and submission artifacts.

TEAM

KernelCrew — Manuel Guerrero and Jessica Garay
